title: From Failure to Insight: Analyzing Disk Breakdowns in Large-Scale HPC Environments
problem: Disk failures in large-scale HPC storage systems impact reliability and operational efficiency. Understanding failure patterns across temporal, spatial, and relational dimensions is essential for improving storage robustness and system design.
motivation: Preventing disk failures and enhancing storage robustness is critical for reliable, cost-effective operation of large-scale HPC data centers.
method: The researchers collected real-world disk failure data from large-scale HPC storage systems (computer systems used for scientific computing) over five years, recording 5,000+ individual failures from 40,000+ disks. They examined these failures in three ways: when they happened over time, where they occurred in the storage system, and how one failure connected to or predicted others. This revealed patterns in how storage systems actually break down under real conditions—information that helps engineers design more reliable systems.
key_novelty: Five years of actual disk failure data from 40,000+ disks in production HPC systems reveals patterns that guide more reliable storage design.
contributions: Large-scale disk failure datasets from production HPC environments (5,000+ records from 40,000+ disks over 5 years)
Comprehensive temporal, spatial, and relational failure pattern analysis
Reliability assessment methodology for HPC storage systems
Actionable insights for HPC storage system design and deployment
limitations: Study focuses on specific HPC environments; generalizability to other storage architectures and disk technologies not discussed.
primary_theme: Storage reliability and failure prevention in HPC
